VISAKA INDUSTRIES Q2 FY27: REVENUE UP 22.8% YOY, EBITDA SURGES 208%; PAT TURNS POSITIVE, TARGETS 10–15% REVENUE CAGR & 10–12% EBITDA MARGINS BY FY29, V-NEXT AND SOLAR ROOFING TO DRIVE GROWTH

• Net Profit: Reported PAT of ₹71.3 Cr versus loss of ₹8.7 Cr YoY, including ₹68.7 Cr exceptional income.

• H1 FY27 Performance: Revenue grew 19.1% YoY to ₹989.3 Cr; EBITDA surged 102.9% to ₹127.6 Cr.

• FY29 Growth Outlook: 10–15% revenue CAGR and EBITDA margin improvement towards 10–12%.

• Building Products: Q2 revenue increased to ₹331 Cr from ₹266 Cr YoY, with segment EBIT rising to ₹30 Cr from ₹8 Cr.

• Synthetic Yarn: Q2 revenue grew to ₹68 Cr from ₹59 Cr YoY, with EBIT improving to ₹5 Cr from ₹2 Cr.

• V-Next Growth Strategy: Cement fibre boards and panels remain the primary growth engine, supported by capacity expansion, innovation and market penetration.

• Cement Fibre Boards: Installed capacity stands at 3.56 lakh tonnes annually, with 86% utilisation in FY26.

• Cement Roofing: Annual capacity of 8.48 lakh tonnes, with approximately 18% domestic market share.

• ATUM Solar Roofing: Emerging growth business with 30 MW manufacturing capacity and international market opportunities.

• Product Diversification: Non-asbestos and value-added products contribute approximately 47% of revenue, reducing dependence on traditional roofing.

• Balance Sheet: Net debt-to-equity improved to 0.3x in FY26, with continued focus on deleveraging and cash generation.

• Management Outlook: Focused on expanding V-Next, scaling integrated solar roofing, improving operating leverage, increasing value-added product contribution and strengthening profitability through FY29.

PAGE INDUSTRIES Q2: FEMA NON-COMPLIANCE FLAGGED; SEEKS GOVERNMENT APPROVAL 🔴

• Regulatory Issue: Company disclosed non-compliance with FEMA rules relating to retail trading of imported Jockey and Speedo products through e-commerce

• Nature of Violation: Online retailing of imported products from multiple brands without physical retail stores was not in accordance with applicable foreign investment rules

• RBI Application: Company applied to RBI for compounding of the non-compliance on May 20, 2026

• RBI Response: On October 16, 2026, RBI returned the application, advising the company to first obtain post-facto approval from the Government of India

• Next Steps: Management is seeking government approval and plans to reapply to RBI for compounding thereafter

• Financial Impact: Management expects any financial impact to be immaterial

• Accounting Treatment: No adjustment made to financial results, based on management's assessment

• Regulatory Status: Matter remains unresolved, pending government approval and subsequent RBI compounding

HD FIRE PROTECT Q2 FY27: REVENUE UP 28.8% YOY, EBITDA RISES 29.2%, PAT JUMPS 41%; H2 EXPECTED STRONGER, JALGAON-THANE CAPACITY EXPANSION & SAUDI ARABIA MARKET EXPANSION IN FOCUS

• H2 FY27 Outlook: Management expects stronger second-half performance, with H2 historically contributing 55–60% of annual revenue due to higher Q4 project closures.

• Capacity Expansion: Expanding Jalgaon manufacturing facilities, including a dedicated fire-testing laboratory, industrial warehouse and R&D centre.

• Thane Expansion: Constructing a new production facility and warehouse at Wagle Estate to increase capacity and reduce lead times.

• Saudi Arabia Expansion: Established a subsidiary to strengthen local presence and participate in Saudi infrastructure and industrial projects.

• Saudi Aramco Opportunities: Jalgaon facility holds 9COM registration for valves and sprinkler systems, enabling participation in upcoming Saudi Aramco RFQs.

• Global Business: Exports contributed 35.6% of H1 FY27 revenue, with products supplied to over 90 countries.

• New Product Launches: Introduced UL-listed K11.2 fire sprinklers, FM-approved air-release valves and UL-listed pressure gauges during H1 FY27.

• Regulatory Certifications: Holds 21 UL listings and 87 FM approvals, strengthening access to high-entry-barrier international markets.

• R&D Expansion: Developing advanced deluge valves and fluorine-free foam suppression systems, supported by eight patent/design registrations filed or granted.

• Operating Cash Flow: H1 FY27 operating cash flow reached ₹71.07 Cr, reflecting strong cash generation.

• Management Outlook: Positive on domestic infrastructure demand, international market expansion, new product development and manufacturing capacity additions, while monitoring raw material price volatility and logistics costs.

MAN INDUSTRIES Q2 FY27: RECORD EBITDA UP 86.6% YOY, PAT SURGES 121.7%; ₹3,500 CR ORDER BOOK, ₹320 CR REVENUE DEFERRED, ₹110 MN US CAPEX & JAMMU-DAMMAM EXPANSIONS ON TRACK

• Consolidated Revenue: Increased 45.1% YoY to ₹1,210 Cr, up 14.9% QoQ.

• EBITDA: Surged 86.6% YoY to ₹190 Cr, achieving highest-ever quarterly EBITDA, with margin at 15.6%.

• Net Profit: Jumped 121.7% YoY to ₹82 Cr, up 33.5% QoQ.

• Order Book: Strong consolidated order book of approximately ₹3,500 Cr across India and Saudi Arabia, with majority executable over the next 6–9 months.

• Revenue Deferral: Approximately ₹320 Cr revenue deferred due to Strait of Hormuz shipping disruptions; shipments now being executed through alternative ports.

• NPC Acquisition: Saudi Arabia's National Pipe Company contributed approximately ₹532 Cr revenue and ₹94 Cr EBITDA from May 21 to September 30, 2026.

• NPC Quarterly Performance: Q3 CY26 revenue reached ₹486 Cr, with EBITDA of ₹88 Cr and margin of approximately 18%.

• Jammu Expansion: Greenfield stainless steel seamless pipe plant progressing, with production expected by April 2027.

• Dammam Facility: Saudi Arabia coating and double-jointing facility targeted to commence operations by March 2027.

• US Manufacturing Expansion: Plans $110 Mn investment in a 350,000 MTPA HSAW pipe manufacturing facility through its wholly owned subsidiary.

• Real Estate Project: Merino Shelters' Navi Mumbai project launched in October 2026, with expected cash flows of ₹700–800 Cr over 5–6 years.

• Manufacturing Capacity: Combined installed capacity exceeds 1.6 million MTPA following NPC acquisition.

• Management Outlook: Positive on order execution, deferred shipment recovery, NPC integration and global capacity expansion, strengthening its position as an integrated pipeline solutions provider.

AUTOLINE : WINS NEW TATA MOTORS PV BUSINESS WORTH OVER RS 180 CR

• New business awards from Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles for hatchback and SUV components, covering both ICE and EV applications
• Awards carry estimated annual incremental revenue potential of ~₹180 Cr plus one-time tooling revenue potential of ~₹30 Cr
• Q2 FY27 revenue from operations at ₹304.59 Cr, up 75.75% YoY; EBITDA at ₹24.88 Cr, up 46.44% YoY
• Q2 FY27 PAT at ₹6.70 Cr vs ₹2.78 Cr YoY; EBITDA margin at 8.17% vs 9.80% YoY
• Targets ~30%-40% revenue CAGR growth for FY27, with EBITDA margin expected to rise to ~10% plus
Impact: Positive (Tata Motors ICE and EV programmes add ~₹180 Cr annual revenue potential, improving growth visibility despite current margin pressure)

RADHAGOBIND COMMERCIAL : COC APPROVES RESOLUTION PLAN WITH 100% VOTES

• Committee of Creditors approved the resolution plan with 100% voting share, above the Section 30(4) threshold
• E-voting on the plan ran from 6:00 p.m. on 06-11-2026 to 6:00 p.m. on 07-11-2026 after the 12th CoC meeting on 04-11-2026
• Resolution Professional to file the CoC-approved plan with NCLT Kolkata under Section 30(6) for approval under Section 31
• CIRP was initiated by NCLT Kolkata order dated 30-10-2025 in CP (IB) No. 71/KB/2025
• BSE and Calcutta Stock Exchange, operational creditors, were given minutes of the 12th CoC meeting
Impact: Positive (100% CoC approval moves the company closer to exiting CIRP, though NCLT sanction is still pending)

AFSL : TO INCORPORATE 100% SUBSIDIARY IN HONG KONG FOR BULLION TRADING

• Board approved incorporation of a subsidiary/step-down subsidiary in Hong Kong with 100% shareholding of the company
• Proposed entity to trade bullion in international markets along with trading in securities, commodities and commodity derivatives
• Consideration is cash; subscription price as per constitutional documents of the proposed entity
• Whole-Time Director & CEO Chintan Natwarlal Mehta resigned with immediate effect from November 11, 2026, citing no material reason
• Mayank Mahesh Mundhra appointed Additional Director (Whole-Time), liable to retire by rotation, subject to shareholder approval
Impact: Neutral (Hong Kong bullion trading vehicle widens international footprint, but abrupt CEO exit and pending incorporation keep near-term impact unclear)

POWERGRID : WINS RS 243.34 CR TBCB PROJECT

• Declared successful bidder under Tariff Based Competitive Bidding for an Intra-State Transmission System project in Karnataka
• Scope covers 3X500MVA 400/220kV sub-station at Humnabad in Bidar District plus 400kV and 220kV transmission lines and associated bays
• Project to be built on Build, Own, Operate and Transfer (BOOT) basis at quoted Annual Transmission Charges of ₹243.34 Cr
• Letter of Intent dated 10th November 2026 received by the company on 11th November 2026
• With this win, POWERGRID has secured 11 TBCB transmission projects in FY 2026-27 till date, with cumulative Annual Transmission Charges of ₹8,106.97 Cr
Impact: Positive (Adds a regulated-return transmission asset to the TBCB order book and takes FY27 TBCB wins to 11 projects)

CUPID LIMITED Q2 FY27: RAISES FY27 REVENUE GUIDANCE TO ₹880 CR+ & PAT TO ₹275 CR+; TARGETS ₹1,950 CR REVENUE BY FY29, ₹400 CR V2 RETAIL OPPORTUNITY & PALAVA CAPACITY EXPANSION

• FY27 Revenue Guidance: Raised to ₹880 Cr+ from ₹800 Cr+, with PAT guidance increased to ₹275 Cr+ from ₹250 Cr+.

• FY28 Guidance: Targets revenue of ₹1,305 Cr+ and approximately ₹390 Cr net profit.

• FY29 Guidance: Targets revenue of ₹1,950 Cr+ and approximately ₹605 Cr net profit.

• H2 FY27 Outlook: Management expects the strongest-ever second half, supported by Palava commissioning and retail expansion.

• Style Baazar Partnership: Expects approximately ₹200 Cr revenue contribution in FY27; retail network targeted to exceed 500 stores within 2–3 years.

• V2 Retail Partnership: Expects approximately ₹400 Cr revenue over the next 12 months, with exclusive 400 sq. ft. retail space across 425+ stores by mid-December 2026.

• Palava Expansion: Commissioning targeted in Q3 FY27, increasing annual male condom capacity from 480 million to approximately 1.25 billion and female condom capacity from 52 million to approximately 125 million.

• IVD Capacity Expansion: Targets doubling diagnostic kit production capacity from approximately 4 lakh to 8 lakh kits per day by December 2027.

• Domestic Distribution: Targets presence in 4,000+ modern trade stores during FY27, supported by 1,850+ distributors and over 2 lakh retail outlets.

• Export Business: Implemented a minimum 10% price increase across its export portfolio; targets approximately 35% expansion in international market footprint.

• South Africa Business: Supplies approximately 153 million male condoms and 23.4 million female condoms annually under the 2025–30 programme.

• New Manufacturing Ventures: Exploring an asset-light South Africa JV with up to 49% ownership and a proposed West Bengal manufacturing project, both subject to further approvals and evaluation.

• IVD Business: Expects sizeable state government orders and international tender opportunities following EU IVDR certification for four diagnostic kits.

• Debt Outlook: Management intends to make the company debt-free while continuing business expansion and strategic investments.

**Announcement** 📢

**Veefin Solutions has officially commenced trading on the NSE and BSE main boards!**

What makes this particularly interesting is that the company is simultaneously making a strategic shift towards AI with its new identity, **veefin.ai**.

Building on its enterprise technology business, Veefin is expanding into AI with AIOS, a platform that deploys digital employees across industries and business functions. It has already developed over 1,000 reusable AI skills and begun internal deployments.

Another interesting aspect is its financial performance. For H1 FY27, Veefin reported:

• Group Revenue: ₹238.82 crore, up 116.2%
• Group PAT: ₹24.85 crore, up 126.6%
• Standalone Revenue: ₹49.19 crore, up 83.6%
• Standalone PAT: ₹13.97 crore, up 79.4%

An interesting combination of strong business growth, main board listing and an ambitious AI strategy.

Definitely a company worth keeping on the radar.

CITI on Bharti Airtel ; Buy, TP Rs 2390

In a notable reversal, Bharti has reinstated its Rs299 recharge plan 3 months after withdrawing it in Aug'26.

While earlier plan offered 1.5 GB/day of data, relaunched version provides 1 GB/day.

Move reflects Bharti's response to competitive pressures, as peers did not follow its earlier tariff action, as well as elevated churn during 2Q.

Churn increased from 2.6% to 2.9% qoq, resulting in net subscriber additions slowing sharply qoq from +3.3m to +0.7m

Decision underscores challenges of implementing unilateral tariff actions in prepaid smartphone segment, where competitive intensity remains highest

It suggests that pricing discipline is difficult to sustain without broader industry participation.

Note that based on certain assumptions around Bharti's subscriber mix, had estimated the Aug'26 move could potentially benefit ARPU by c.Rs4/mth (EPS benefit of c.2%).

Bharti recently reported ARPU improvement from Rs264 to Rs271 in 2Q.

• Citi sees limited upside in LME aluminium prices from current levels.

GOLDMAN SACHS ON TATA STEEL ; MAINTAINS NEUTRAL, TARGET PRICE ₹215 (CMP ₹190.20)

• Domestic operations remain highly efficient, while European operations continue to face uncertainty.

• India steel realisations expected to rise ₹3,500/tonne QoQ, offsetting higher coking coal costs.

• FY27 European cost savings could face challenges due to lower production volumes.

• Net Debt/EBITDA at 2.4x remains within management's 2.5x guidance.

• Domestic profitability expected to increasingly depend on downstream product mix until NINL capacity expansion by FY30.

CLSA ON ONGC ; HIGH CONVICTION OUTPERFORM, TARGET PRICE ₹405 (CMP ₹234.80)

• Q2 standalone net profit missed estimates by 5% due to impairment losses and a one-off provision.

• EBITDA and core PBT beat estimates by 7% and 4%, respectively.

• Declared interim dividend of ₹8/share, implying a 3.5% dividend yield.

• KG-98/2 and Daman projects expected to drive production volume growth in FY27–28.

• CLSA sees 76% upside potential based on its assumption of Brent crude at $82/barrel in FY28.

CITI ON GLAND PHARMA ; MAINTAINS SELL, TARGET PRICE ₹2,360 (CMP ₹3,132.80)

• Citi believes current valuations already factor in significant growth and margin improvement.

• EMPS margins benefited from a one-off write-back, while the engineering business remained strong.

• October price hikes expected to support UCP margin improvement from Q4.

THERMAX – JEFFERIES

• Jefferies maintains BUY, cuts target price to ₹4,020 (CMP: ₹2,839.80).

• Q2 EBITDA missed estimates by 19%, while EBITDA margin at 6.9% was 170 bps below expectations.

• Commodity inflation and shipment delays weighed on performance.

• H1 order inflows declined 4% YoY, though management expects a recovery in H2 FY27.

• Order book grew 16% YoY, supporting revenue visibility through FY27–29.

• Jefferies cuts FY27–30 EPS estimates by 1–22%.

HONASA CONSUMER – JEFFERIES

• Jefferies maintains BUY, raises target price to ₹700 (CMP: ₹470.05).

• Delivered its strongest growth since listing, with revenue and EBITDA doubling YoY.

• Mamaearth grew in high teens, while The Derma Co and newer brands scaled rapidly.

• Distribution expansion and product innovation expected to support future growth.

• Jefferies raises earnings estimates by 10–16%.

HINDALCO – CITI

• Citi maintains NEUTRAL, cuts target price to ₹1,050 (CMP: ₹953).

• Q2 consolidated EBITDA rose 42% YoY but declined 8% QoQ.

• India upstream EBITDA stood at ₹7,000 Cr, downstream at ₹330 Cr, copper at ₹1,670 Cr and Novelis at ₹4,860 Cr.

• Net Debt/EBITDA improved to 1.8x from 1.95x earlier.

• Novelis insurance recovery reached $1.3 billion, including $900 million already received.

• India costs expected to rise further in Q3, while expansion benefits remain back-ended.

• Citi sees limited upside in LME aluminium prices from current levels.

TATA STEEL – GOLDMAN SACHS

• Goldman Sachs maintains NEUTRAL with a target price of ₹215 (CMP: ₹190.20).

• Domestic operations remain highly efficient, while European operations continue to face uncertainty.

• India steel realisations expected to increase by ₹3,500/tonne QoQ, offsetting higher coking coal costs.

• FY27 European cost savings may face challenges due to lower production volumes.

• Net Debt/EBITDA at 2.4x remains within management's guidance of 2.5x.

• Domestic profitability increasingly depends on downstream product mix until NINL capacity expansion by FY30.

ONGC – CLSA

• CLSA maintains HIGH CONVICTION OUTPERFORM with a target price of ₹405 (CMP: ₹234.80).

• Q2 standalone net profit missed estimates by 5% due to impairment losses and a one-off provision.

• EBITDA and core PBT beat estimates by 7% and 4%, respectively.

• Declared an interim dividend of ₹8/share, implying a 3.5% dividend yield.

• KG-98/2 and Daman projects expected to drive production growth in FY27–28.

• CLSA sees 76% upside potential, assuming Brent crude averages $82/barrel in FY28.

Curious when FII will come back to India

So gave Co-pilot a prompt
“Why FIIs wont return to India even as AI trade unwind globally”

Reverse Psychology

Here is the response

1. India is still expensive vs EM peers
o Even after corrections, India trades at a premium to most emerging markets.
o FIIs compare India with China, Korea, Taiwan, Brazil, not with India's own history.
o If China is at 10-12x PE and India at 20-25x PE, capital tends to chase cheaper markets. 
2. India lacks direct AI beneficiaries
o The AI trade created winners in US tech, Taiwan semiconductors and Korean memory-chip companies.
o India has very few large listed AI, semiconductor or hyperscaler plays that global thematic funds can buy. 
3. Dollar returns matter, not rupee returns
o FIIs think in USD.
o Even if Nifty is flat or slightly up, rupee depreciation can wipe out returns.
o Currency risk remains a major deterrent for foreign capital. 
4. US yields remain a strong competitor
o If US Treasuries offer attractive risk-free returns, FIIs need a much higher expected return from India.
o Many global allocators prefer earning 4-5% in dollar assets rather than taking EM risk. 
5. India's earnings growth has moderated
o India's premium valuation was justified when earnings were compounding rapidly.
o If earnings growth slows while valuations remain rich, FIIs question the risk-reward. 
6. Better opportunities elsewhere
o Korea, Taiwan and China offer exposure to AI, semiconductors and manufacturing at lower valuations.
o Global funds have finite capital; India is competing against these markets for allocation. 
7. India is no longer an under-owned market
o After years of strong inflows, most EM funds already have meaningful India exposure.
o Incremental flows require a new catalyst, not just the absence of AI enthusiasm.
8. Domestic flows reduce urgency
o SIPs, mutual funds and insurance money continue supporting Indian markets despite FII selling.
o Paradoxically, this resilience prevents large valuation corrections that would otherwise attract FIIs back.

Maruti Suzuki India should be rechristened as Suzuki India

Maruti's journey started as a Govt of India project. Maruti Udyog was the Indian promoter & Suzuki was brought in as the technology partner. Back then, this was very much an Indian company with Japanese know-how.

Over time, the Indian promoter gradually diluted its holding & eventually exited completely. Suzuki did the opposite, staying invested through every cycle & steadily increasing its stake.

What began as a JV slowly became Suzuki's most important global asset. The ownership story itself tells you who has deepened commitment over the decades.

For years, investors debated why Suzuki was setting up fresh manufacturing capacity outside Maruti Suzuki through its Gujarat subsidiary instead of housing it directly in the listed entity.

Then came the reversal. Suzuki transferred Suzuki Motor Gujarat into Maruti Suzuki at a valuation of roughly ₹12,000+ Cr. Rather than taking cash, it largely took equity.

The result? Suzuki's ownership in Maruti Suzuki moved up further without having to buy equivalent shares from the secondary market.

This wasn't just a restructuring exercise. It was Suzuki effectively converting manufacturing assets into a larger stake in India's largest PV company.

Even after that transaction, Suzuki did not stop. It has periodically picked up additional shares from the open market whenever opportunities emerged.

The message is clear. The Indian promoter exited long ago. The Japanese promoter keeps doubling down on India.

Look at the cars on the road today. The branding emphasis is on the giant "S" logo. 10-15years back, cars started selling with only “S” logo, 1st on premium nexa cars, then on all the models. You will hardly see Maruti branded cars on road now

For many younger buyers, the brand recall is shifting from "Maruti Suzuki" to simply "Suzuki". The transition is subtle but visible.

India is now the crown jewel of Suzuki Motor Corp. A substantial portion of Suzuki valuation come from Indian listed entity. Maruti $38bn mcap translate to $21bn (for 58% stake, $15bn if applied 30% Holdco disc).

Even beyond that, Maruti pays over $500m to Suzuki as royalty, that value must be over $5bn in the SoTP of Suzuki motors. Suzuki motors also have successful 2w biz in India, they are 6th largest 2w in India, clocking over 1lac units every month

In many ways, investors buying Suzuki Motor Corp are indirectly buying the India story. Cars sold by Suzuki in India is higher than overall car sold by Suzuki in other 100 countries combined

A rebranding to "Suzuki India" could also help shed the old "cheap small-car company" perception. As premium SUVs, hybrids & future EVs gain share, a stronger global MNC identity may command a different customer mindset.

Ownership, capital allocation, manufacturing integration, branding & growth strategy all point in one direction: this is increasingly Suzuki's India story.

Conclusion: Maruti only stays in Co. name hence should be renamed now
